question.text: Mr. X is 41 years old with a Rs. 100 crore portfolio and a 40% cap on any single asset class. He is choosing between Fund A (a long-short small-cap Cat III AIF) and Fund B (a market-neutral Cat III AIF with overseas exposure) for a Rs. 20 crore allocation. Which allocation is consistent with the workbook example?

answer.text: Allocate the full Rs. 20 crore to another domestic equity fund
Allocate the full Rs. 20 crore to Fund B, or split the Rs. 20 crore between Fund A and Fund B, to manage concentration and add international diversification
Allocate to a domestic real estate fund only

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 38-39 of the workbook, Mr. X (aged 41, Rs. 100 crore portfolio, 40% asset-class cap) may allocate his Rs. 20 crore entirely to Fund B (market-neutral with overseas exposure) or split it between Fund A and Fund B, in order to manage concentration and add international diversification. The Trap: Adding another domestic equity fund increases correlation; gold and real estate shift asset class but do not use Cat III strategies. Note: The workbook (page 247) describes Cat III strategies that can be used for this kind of diversification overlay.
